name: HS3003 humidity & temperature sensor
description: Renesas HS3003 relative humidity (0–100 %RH, ±2.5 %RH typical, 20–80 %RH) and temperature (-40 to 125 °C, ±0.25 °C typical, 0–70 °C) sensor with 14-bit results over I2C at fixed address 0x44; a zero-length write starts a measurement and a 4-byte read fetches it (status bits, no CRC). The chip runs on 2.3–5.5 V. Sold as: MikroElektronika Temp&Hum 18 Click (MIKROE-4892), a mikroBUS board with two 8-pin headers (AN, RST, CS, SCK, MISO, MOSI, 3V3, GND / PWM, INT, TX, RX, SCL, SDA, 5V, GND; only 3V3, GND, SCL and SDA are needed), 4.7 kΩ I2C pull-ups, a VCC SEL jumper (3V3 / 5V) and a power LED.
eli5: Tells your board how damp the air is and how warm it is.

buildNotes: Start a measurement with a zero-length write to 0x44 (address + W, then STOP: i2c.writeto(0x44, b'')); there is no command byte.
Wait at least 33.9 ms (14-bit RH and T, the factory default), then read 4 bytes: status + humidity[13:8], humidity[7:0], temperature[13:6], temperature[5:0] + 2 undefined bits.
Status bits 7:6 of the first byte: 00 = new valid data, 01 = stale (already read or not finished); fetch again after a short wait.
Keep the VCC SEL jumper on 3V3 and power the board from the 3V3 pin: the SDA/SCL pull-ups go to the selected VCC, so the 5V setting would put 5 V on an ESP32's or Pico's I2C pins.
Only 3V3, GND, SCL and SDA are used; the other mikroBUS pins are not connected on this board.

driver.code:
# HS3003 humidity & temperature sensor (Renesas HS300x series), MicroPython driver.
# Protocol from the Renesas HS300x datasheet (section 6):
#  - Measurement Request (MR): the 7-bit address with the WRITE bit and NO data bytes (zero-length write).
#  - Wait for the conversion: 33.90 ms for 14-bit RH + 14-bit T (factory default), including wake-up.
#  - Data Fetch (DF): read 4 bytes. Byte 0 bits 7:6 = status (00 valid, 01 stale), then humidity[13:0]
#    big-endian; bytes 2-3 = temperature[15:2] big-endian, the 2 LSBs of byte 3 are undefined (masked off).
#  - RH = H / (2^14 - 1) * 100 %RH;  T = T / (2^14 - 1) * 165 - 40 degC.
# No CRC: the status bits are the only validity check.
import time

ADDR = 0x44            # fixed address (datasheet 6.2)
_MEAS_MS = 34          # 33.90 ms at 14-bit / 14-bit resolution
_STATUS_STALE = 0x01


class HS3003:
    def __init__(self, i2c, addr=ADDR):
        self.i2c = i2c
        self.addr = addr

    def _request(self):
        # Measurement Request: address + W, then STOP (no command byte).
        self.i2c.writeto(self.addr, b'')

    def _fetch(self):
        d = self.i2c.readfrom(self.addr, 4)
        status = d[0] >> 6
        h_raw = ((d[0] & 0x3F) << 8) | d[1]
        t_raw = ((d[2] << 8) | d[3]) >> 2
        return status, h_raw, t_raw

    def read(self):
        """Measure once and return (temperature in degC, relative humidity in %)."""
        self._request()
        time.sleep_ms(_MEAS_MS + 6)  # margin over the 33.9 ms measurement time
        for _ in range(5):
            status, h_raw, t_raw = self._fetch()
            if status != _STATUS_STALE:
                break
            time.sleep_ms(10)  # conversion not finished yet: fetch again
        else:
            raise OSError('HS3003 returned stale data: check the wiring and the supply')
        rh = h_raw * 100 / 16383
        t = t_raw * 165 / 16383 - 40
        return t, rh

    def temperature(self):
        return self.read()[0]

    def humidity(self):
        return self.read()[1]

example.code:
from machine import I2C, Pin
import time
from hs3003 import HS3003

i2c = I2C({I2C_ID}, sda=Pin({SDA}), scl=Pin({SCL}))
sensor = HS3003(i2c)
while True:
    t, h = sensor.read()
    print('T=%.1fC H=%.0f%%' % (t, h))
    time.sleep(1)
